name: What kind of warranty should I expect for a new residential roof?

mainEntity.name: What kind of warranty should I expect for a new residential roof?

acceptedAnswer.text: A new residential roof typically comes with two types of warranties: a manufacturer's warranty on the materials and a contractor's warranty on the workmanship. Manufacturer warranties vary by material but often range from 20 years for basic asphalt shingles up to 50 years or a lifetime for premium products like architectural shingles, tile, or metal. Workmanship warranties, provided by the contractor, usually cover installation defects for 5 to 10 years. Always review warranty details carefully to understand coverage, limitations, and transferability.
acceptedAnswer.description: Expect a manufacturer's warranty on materials (20-50+ years) and a contractor's warranty on workmanship (5-10 years). Review all details carefully.
